When water solidifies, it expands in volume

The volume of the water increases on freezing

explanation: Water pressure falls as the bubble rises, so the trapped air expands and the bubble grows (Boyle's law). Off-topic (physics), moved.

It contains more water which has higher specific heat
It is more green in colour which does reflects atmospheric heat
It has thicker skin which would not allow penetration of heat

exam: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
q: What happens when salt is added to boiling water?
options: The water will boil more and temperature of the water would fall
The Water will stop boiling and the temperature of the water would fall
The water will stop boiling and temperature of the water would rise
The water will boil more and the temperature of the water would rise
key_text: The water will stop boiling and temperature of the water would rise
explanation: Salt raises the boiling point, so the water stops boiling for a moment and its temperature rises to the new, higher boiling point before it boils again. Off-topic (physics), moved.

options: Melting point has no relation with pressure
explanation: Pressure lowers the melting point of ice (regelation); the skate's pressure melts a thin water layer. Off-topic (physics), moved.

options: The boiling point decreases and freezing point increases.
The boiling point increases and freezing point decreases.
Both the boiling point and the freezing point increase.
Both the boiling point and freezing point decrease.

explanation: A dissolved salt raises the boiling point and lowers the freezing point of water (colligative properties). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

explanation: Naphthalene mothballs pass straight from solid to vapour – sublimation. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

exam: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
q: During winter in cold countries, the following is mixed to melt the ice on the roads?
explanation: Salt (rock salt) spread on roads lowers the freezing point of water and melts ice. Off-topic (everyday chemistry), moved.

exam: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
q: When ice is melting its temperature would?
explanation: While ice melts, the heat supplied goes into latent heat of fusion, so its temperature stays constant at 0°C. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
q: The shortest path between the initial and final position is known as
explanation: Displacement is the shortest straight-line path between the initial and final positions; distance is the actual path length. Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

exam: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
q: Which liquid is represented by the Volume-Temperature Curve? (The curve shows volume falling from 0°C to a minimum at 4°C and rising again up to 10°C.)
explanation: Water contracts from 0°C to 4°C (maximum density) and expands above it – the anomalous expansion of water.

exam: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
q: Which of the following is responsible for slowing down a moving object?
explanation: Friction is the force that opposes motion and slows a moving object.

exam: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
q: Which of the following is NOT an example of gravity?
options: Revolution of planets around the sun
A rock rolling down a hill
Formation of tides in the ocean
explanation: Writing with a pencil works by friction, not gravity; planetary revolution, a rock rolling downhill and tides are effects of gravity.

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
q: A boat filled with heavy stones is in a lake. If the stones are thrown into the lake, the level of water with respect to the boat would?
explanation: A floating boat displaces water equal to the stones' weight; sunk, the stones displace only their volume, so the lake level falls (and the lighter boat rides higher).

exam: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
q: Which of the following materials is not commonly used as sound-proof material?
explanation: Rockwool, wood and (double/laminated) glass are used for sound insulation; plain iron sheets reflect and transmit sound and are not a sound-proofing material.

exam: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main

options: Copper is not a harmful metal
Copper is better conductor of heat than steel
Oil stains on Copper are easier to clean
key_text: Copper is better conductor of heat than steel
explanation: Copper conducts heat much better than steel, so a copper bottom spreads heat quickly and evenly.

exam: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran

explanation: Levers are of three classes (fulcrum, load or effort in the middle). Physics of simple machines, not ICT.

exam: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab

explanation: Pure water has a density of about 1 g/cm3 (1,000 kg/m3), highest at 4 °C.

exam: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
q: What should be the size of the burner of the gas stove to save the consumption of LPG?
options: Size of the burner does not matter
explanation: A small burner saves LPG because its flame stays under the vessel's base. A large flame spills heat around the sides. (Off-topic: energy saving in daily life.)

exam: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
q: If a balloon filled with air is immersed in hot water, its volume would
explanation: Air expands when heated (Charles's law), so a balloon in hot water swells and its volume increases. (Off-topic: physics.)

exam: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
q: If egg shell is carefully dissolved in acid and then immersed in salt water, then the shell?
explanation: Acid dissolves the calcium carbonate shell, leaving the semi-permeable membrane; in strong salt water (hypertonic) water leaves the egg by osmosis, so it shrinks. Off-topic science, moved.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: Temperature and time used to sterilise glassware in hot air oven
explanation: A hot air oven sterilises glassware at 160°C with a holding time of one hour (170°C for 30 min, 180°C for 20 min); shorter times at 160°C are not enough. Off-topic (microbiology).

exam: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
q: Humans have ____ of chromosomes, or tightly wrapped strands of DNA, that provide the instructions for metabolic processes, building cellular and tissue components, as well as other body functions.
explanation: Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs (22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes). Off-topic (biology).

explanation: Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP releases about 30.5 kJ/mol (7.3 kcal/mol) under standard conditions.

exam: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)

explanation: Human cells have 46 chromosomes: 22 pairs (44) of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes.

explanation: Genes for body characters are carried by both sperms and eggs, which each pass one set of chromosomes.

explanation: Magnesium is the central metal ion of chlorophyll. Off-topic (biology).

explanation: Humans have two sex chromosomes, X and Y (XX female, XY male); Z belongs to the ZW system of birds.

exam: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
q: What is the full form of ATP?
explanation: ATP is Adenosine Triphosphate: adenosine (adenine + ribose) with three phosphate groups, the cell's energy currency. 'Adenine' alone lacks the ribose, and 'protease' is an enzyme class.

exam: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
q: What is known as the 'energy molecule' in the living World?
explanation: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the energy currency of the cell. TNT is an explosive, ADP is its spent form and DNA is the genetic material.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
q: Which organelle is called power house of the cell?
explanation: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell: they release energy as ATP by cellular respiration.

exam: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
q: Which of the following part of a cell is called power house of energy?
explanation: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell; the nucleus controls the cell and vacuoles store substances.

exam: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
q: If mitochondria is removed from a living cell?
options: Energy metabolism of the cell gets extinguished
Cell fluid would not be transported
key_text: Energy metabolism of the cell gets extinguished
explanation: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration and ATP production, so removing them stops the cell's energy metabolism. Reproduction and transport would only fail as a later result.

exam: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
q: The occurrence of differences in characteristics among individuals of the same species is called
explanation: Differences in characters among individuals of the same species are called variation. Inheritance is passing on traits, evolution the long-term change and adaptation a fit to the habitat.

exam: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main

explanation: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and CO2 without oxygen, so fermentation is anaerobic respiration.

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
q: The limit of growth is fixed by which of the following factor?
explanation: The limit of growth is fixed by internal (genetic, hormonal) factors of the organism; nutrition and exercise only help reach it.

exam: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
q: Sweating is an
options: Difficult to state, which type of process it is
explanation: Sweat cools the body because its evaporation absorbs heat from the skin, so sweating is an endothermic process.

exam: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
q: Respiration is an
explanation: Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy, so it is an exothermic process.

exam: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
q: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is a/an?
explanation: Composting is microbial oxidation of organic matter and releases heat (compost heaps warm up), so it is exothermic.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P

explanation: Yeast and Hydra reproduce asexually by budding; Amoeba and Paramecium divide by binary fission.

exam: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
q: In humans, which cells can perform anaerobic respiration during oxygen shortage?
explanation: Skeletal muscle cells respire anaerobically in oxygen shortage, producing lactic acid.

exam: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
q: Which of the following is present in plant cells but not cells of animals?
explanation: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, which animal cells lack; both have vacuoles, plasma membrane and Golgi.

exam: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis

explanation: Cellulose, the main component of plant cell walls, is the most abundant organic compound on Earth. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

exam: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022

explanation: ATP made in respiration via the electron transport chain is oxidative phosphorylation; photophosphorylation is ATP formation in photosynthesis. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

exam: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
q: In a mammal, what is the ratio of the number of chromosomes in a somatic cell to that in a gamete?
explanation: Somatic cells are diploid (2n, 46 in humans) and gametes haploid (n, 23), so the ratio is 2:1.

exam: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene

exam: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
q: Recently the State of Tamil Nadu banned the sale of cotton candy due to the presence of which cancercausing agent in it?
explanation: Rhodamine B, a textile dye, was found colouring cotton candy; it is carcinogenic, so Tamil Nadu banned the sale (Feb 2024). Aristolochic acid comes from some herbal medicines, benzidine is a dye intermediate and 1,3-butadiene a rubber monomer.

exam: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
q: Which of the following is the most common food preservative against mould, bacteria, fungus and yeast?
explanation: Sorbic acid and its salt potassium sorbate are the commonest preservatives against moulds, yeasts and fungi. Tartaric acid is a food acid, acetylsalicylic acid is aspirin and formic acid only a limited preservative.

exam: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
q: Sodium benzoate is used as a:
explanation: Sodium benzoate (E211) is a food preservative that stops bacteria, yeast and moulds in acidic foods and drinks. It is not a flavour, colour or antacid.

exam: APPSC Group-II Mains 2019 (18-07-2019)
q: What is IQF in food preservations?
explanation: IQF stands for Individually Quick Frozen, a technique where each piece of food is frozen separately and rapidly to keep texture and quality.

exam: APPSC Group-II 2008
q: The gas used for artificial ripening of green fruit is
explanation: Ethylene is the gas (plant hormone) used for artificial ripening of green fruit. Acetylene from calcium carbide only imitates it, and ethane and CO2 do not ripen fruit.

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
q: Which gas is used to ripen fruits?
explanation: Ethylene is the gaseous fruit-ripening hormone.

exam: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
q: To store potato chips for a longer period, the sealed packet of chips is normally filled with which gas?
explanation: Chip packets are flushed with nitrogen, an unreactive gas, so the fats do not get oxidised (rancidity). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: What is the freezing temperature used for preserving pork for long period
explanation: Meat such as pork is stored long-term frozen at about −18°C (0°F) or below; 3–5°C is only chilling. Off-topic (food science), moved.

exam: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
q: Most of the artificial food colouring agents are derived from
explanation: Most synthetic food colours (tartrazine, sunset yellow) are coal-tar (petroleum-derived) dyes. Flowers, fruits and lichens give natural colours.

exam: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
q: Why does open portion of a cut apple turn brown when exposed to air?
options: Due to presence of iron in apple
Due to settling of micro dust present in air
As the original inner colour is brown
Due to oxidation of an enzyme present in apple
key_text: Due to oxidation of an enzyme present in apple
explanation: A cut apple browns because its enzyme polyphenol oxidase, exposed to oxygen, oxidises the fruit's phenolic compounds (enzymatic browning); iron, dust or a brown inner colour are not the cause.

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
q: Rancidity is a/an
explanation: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils, which changes their smell and taste. Antioxidants are added to prevent it.

exam: APPSC AEE Screening Test 2016
q: Natural ripening of climacteric fruits (like apple) occurs due to?
options: Release of ethylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of ethylene and decreased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and decreased rate of respiration
key_text: Release of ethylene and increased rate of respiration
explanation: Climacteric fruits such as apple ripen through a burst of ethylene release and a sharp rise in respiration (the climacteric rise). Acetylene is used only for artificial ripening, and respiration rises rather than falls.

exam: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
q:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
explanation:
Printed key: only (i) follows from the statement. Strictly, both (i) and (ii) are true facts (PMF General Science p.89 / NCERT XI: organ-system level), so a fact-check reading gives 'both'.
The name 'roundworm' comes from the body being circular in cross-section, so conclusion (i) follows from the statement. Conclusion (ii) is a true fact (Aschelminthes have organ-system level of organisation) but does not follow from the statement about the name.

explanation: Insect-eating birds have long, sharp/pointed beaks to pick insects (woodpecker, kingfisher-type); short strong beaks crack seeds. Off-topic (biology), moved.
